banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.name: Cao Bằng coóng phù
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.serving_basis: Four small bowls of hot coóng phù, served as an afternoon treat or winter dessert.
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.description: Coóng phù is a round glutinous-rice dumpling associated with the Tày community in Cao Bằng and is often enjoyed hot in cold weather. Bếp Việt adapts a home version using glutinous-rice flour, ginger and sugarcane molasses; the dumplings are boiled separately before being served in the syrup so it stays clear and fragrant.
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.finished_dish: Soft white rice dumplings sit in amber sugarcane-molasses syrup with warming ginger and a light sprinkle of toasted sesame; the syrup remains clear rather than cloudy.
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.serving: Divide the dumplings and hot ginger-molasses syrup among small bowls. Add toasted sesame or crushed peanuts if desired and serve while warm.
tips: Add warm water gradually until the dough is smooth, pliable and no longer sticky.
Boil the dumplings separately, remove them when they float, then add them to the ginger syrup to keep the syrup clear.
Molasses sweetness varies; dilute and taste it before adding extra sugar.
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.image_alt: A bowl of Cao Bằng coóng phù: soft white rice dumplings in amber ginger and sugarcane-molasses syrup, finished with toasted sesame; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-coong-phu-cao-bang.time_note: About 40 minutes to knead the dough, boil the dumplings and prepare the ginger-molasses syrup.

ingredients.name: Glutinous-rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before mixing; fresh flour gives a tender, chewy texture.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually; the amount depends on the flour's absorption.

ingredients.name: Sugarcane molasses
ingredients.notes: Palm sugar may be used; taste before adjusting.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the ginger syrup.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Crush it and reserve a few thin slices for serving.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: A small pinch balances the sweetness.

ingredients.name: Toasted white sesame
ingredients.notes: Optional topping.

preparation_steps: Combine the glutinous-rice flour and salt. Gradually add warm water and knead for 6–8 minutes until smooth, pliable and not sticky. Cover for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough into small balls about the size of a large marble and place them on a dry tray. Crush the ginger and combine the molasses with the syrup water.
cooking_steps: Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Add the dumplings in batches and stir once. When they float, cook for about 1 more minute, then lift them out to drain.
Simmer the molasses, water, ginger and salt over low heat for 5–7 minutes until fragrant. Taste and adjust; do not reduce it to a candy-like syrup.
Add the cooked dumplings to the ginger syrup and warm for 1–2 minutes. Ladle into bowls, add sesame and serve hot.

thang-den-ha-giang.name: Hà Giang thắng dền
thang-den-ha-giang.serving_basis: Four small bowls, each with 5–6 mung-bean-filled rice dumplings in ginger syrup.
thang-den-ha-giang.description: Thắng dền is a small glutinous-rice dumpling from Hà Giang, commonly filled with mung bean and served in hot ginger-sugar syrup. Bếp Việt prepares a home-style version with a light coconut-milk drizzle, roasted peanuts and shredded coconut; adjust the sweetness to taste.
thang-den-ha-giang.finished_dish: Ivory rice dumplings, some showing their golden mung-bean filling, sit in hot ginger syrup with a restrained coconut-milk drizzle, roasted peanuts and coconut.
thang-den-ha-giang.serving: Divide the dumplings and ginger syrup among bowls. Drizzle with warm coconut milk, add crushed peanuts and shredded coconut, and serve while hot.
tips: Cool the mung-bean filling completely before wrapping; keep each filling ball smaller than its dough wrapper.
Knead until pliable but not wet; if the dough cracks, moisten your hands instead of pouring in a lot of water.
Keep the ginger syrup at a gentle simmer and add the coconut milk only when serving so the ginger remains distinct.
thang-den-ha-giang.image_alt: A bowl of Hà Giang thắng dền: mung-bean-filled rice dumplings in ginger syrup with a light coconut-milk drizzle and roasted peanuts; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
thang-den-ha-giang.time_note: About 1 hour, including steaming the filling, shaping the dumplings and cooking the ginger syrup.

ingredients.name: Glutinous-rice flour
ingredients.notes: Sift before kneading.

ingredients.name: Warm water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually depending on the flour.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak for 2 hours, rinse, then steam or cook until soft and mash.

ingredients.name: Granulated sugar
ingredients.notes: Mix into the mung-bean filling.

ingredients.name: Palm sugar
ingredients.notes: Break into small pieces so it dissolves quickly.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the ginger syrup.

ingredients.name: Mature ginger
ingredients.notes: Crush it; reserve a few slices for serving.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the dough and filling.

ingredients.name: Coconut milk
ingredients.notes: Warm gently without boiling hard.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush and sprinkle on top.

ingredients.name: Shredded coconut
ingredients.notes: Optional topping.

preparation_steps: Soak the mung beans for 2 hours, rinse and steam until soft. Mash while warm with the granulated sugar and a pinch of salt. Cool and roll into 20–24 small balls.
Mix the remaining salt into the glutinous-rice flour. Add warm water gradually and knead until smooth and pliable; divide into 20–24 portions.
Flatten each dough portion, place a mung-bean ball in the center, seal completely and roll smooth. Set the dumplings on a dry tray without touching.
cooking_steps: Simmer the palm sugar, water and crushed ginger over low heat for about 8 minutes until dissolved and fragrant. Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Cook the dumplings in batches; when they float, cook for 1–2 minutes more, then transfer them into the ginger syrup.
Warm the dumplings in the syrup for 2 minutes. Divide into bowls, drizzle with warm coconut milk, add peanuts and coconut, and serve hot.

mi-quang-ech-da-nang.name: Đà Nẵng mì Quảng ếch
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.serving_basis: Four bowls with about 150 g fresh noodles and 2–3 pieces of braised frog per serving, with herbs and rice crackers.
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.description: Mì Quảng ếch is a familiar variation of Đà Nẵng mì Quảng. Frog is marinated and braised with lemongrass, củ nén and turmeric to make a fragrant, concentrated topping. Bếp Việt adapts a home version with just enough broth to moisten the wide noodles, served with fresh herbs, roasted peanuts and sesame rice crackers.
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.finished_dish: Chewy golden turmeric noodles are topped with glossy lemongrass-and-turmeric braised frog and a little concentrated broth; peanuts, fresh herbs and crisp sesame rice crackers add texture.
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.serving: Place the noodles in bowls, top with frog and a little concentrated broth rather than filling the bowl. Serve with fresh herbs, lime, chili, roasted peanuts and sesame rice crackers.
tips: Choose cleaned frog legs from a reputable supplier, pat dry before marinating, and cook fully; keep raw marinade away from ready-to-eat herbs.
Củ nén, also called hành tăm, gives a distinctive aroma; shallots can replace it if needed, though the flavor will differ.
Keep the topping broth concentrated and use only a small amount in each bowl.
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.image_alt: A bowl of Đà Nẵng mì Quảng ếch with golden noodles, lemongrass-and-turmeric braised frog, herbs, peanuts and sesame rice crackers; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
mi-quang-ech-da-nang.time_note: About 1 hour 10 minutes, including marinating, braising and preparing the fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: Cleaned frog legs
ingredients.notes: Buy from a reputable supplier, keep chilled and cook thoroughly.

ingredients.name: Fresh mì Quảng noodles
ingredients.notes: Wide rice noodles; warm briefly if needed.

ingredients.name: Chicken or bone broth
ingredients.notes: Use enough for a concentrated topping, not a full soup bowl.

ingredients.name: Củ nén
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush; shallot may replace part of it.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Mince half and bruise the rest.

ingredients.name: Fresh turmeric
ingredients.notes: Grate or blend; wear gloves to avoid staining.

ingredients.name: Peanut oil
ingredients.notes: Neutral cooking oil can be used instead.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and broth.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: A small amount balances the seasoning.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use freshly ground if available.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Coarsely crushed for serving.

ingredients.name: Mixed fresh herbs and vegetables
ingredients.notes: Young mustard greens, bean sprouts, herbs and banana blossom; wash carefully and drain.

ingredients.name: Sesame rice crackers
ingredients.notes: Break into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Finely sliced.

ingredients.name: Lime and chili
ingredients.notes: Serve separately to taste.

preparation_steps: Check the cleaned frog legs, pat dry and cut into serving pieces. Marinate with half the fish sauce, turmeric, pepper, some of the củ nén and minced lemongrass for 15 minutes; refrigerate if not cooking immediately.
Rinse the fresh herbs under clean running water and drain. Prepare the roasted peanuts, rice crackers, lime, chili and scallions; keep them separate from the raw frog.
cooking_steps: Heat the peanut oil and sauté the remaining củ nén and lemongrass until fragrant. Add the marinated frog and stir until the surface firms.
Add the broth, sugar and remaining fish sauce. Cover and braise gently for 18–22 minutes until the frog is fully cooked and the broth lightly thickens; taste and adjust.

Warm the noodles according to their package instructions. Divide into bowls, add the frog and a small amount of broth, then finish with scallions and peanuts. Serve with herbs, crackers, lime and chili.

lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.name: Hậu Giang fish-cake and bitter-melon hotpot
aliases: Lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua
Bitter melon hotpot with fish cake
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.serving_basis: One small hotpot for four people, served with fresh rice vermicelli or steamed rice.
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.description: Lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua pairs the springy, sweet fish of Hậu Giang with the clean bitterness of bitter melon. Bếp Việt adapts a home hotpot with pork-bone broth, daikon and mushrooms; the fish is kneaded into tender balls and added near serving time.
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.finished_dish: A clear, savory broth holds ivory fish-cake balls and bright green bitter-melon slices; scallions and a little chili add aroma, while the bitterness remains gentle on the finish.
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.serving: Keep the hotpot at a gentle simmer and add bitter melon and other vegetables in small batches to keep them fresh. Serve with rice vermicelli, fish sauce and chili, or steamed rice.
tips: If using pre-ground fish, check the cold chain and ingredients; knead chilled fish in one direction until elastic so the balls hold together.
Season the broth lightly before adding the fish; ground fish may already be seasoned, so taste again after it cooks.
Add bitter melon shortly before serving and avoid overcooking to preserve its green color and gentle bitterness.
search_terms: lẩu cá thát lát khổ qua
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.image_alt: Hậu Giang fish-cake and bitter-melon hotpot with springy ivory fish balls, green bitter-melon slices and clear broth; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
lau-ca-that-lat-kho-qua-hau-giang.time_note: About 1 hour 25 minutes, including simmering the pork-bone broth and preparing the fish balls.

ingredients.name: Fresh featherback fish paste
ingredients.notes: Use freshly scraped chilled fish; check for small bones and a reliable source.

ingredients.name: Bitter melon
ingredients.notes: Halve lengthwise, remove the pith and slice about 5 mm thick.

ingredients.name: Pork bones
ingredients.notes: Blanch briefly and rinse before simmering.

ingredients.name: Daikon
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into rounds.

ingredients.name: Straw or oyster mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Clean; halve larger mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the broth; top up with boiling water if needed.

ingredients.name: Shallots
ingredients.notes: Peel and crush.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the broth and fish; adjust for the saltiness of the fish paste.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Season after skimming the broth.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Mix into the fish paste.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Slice; mix some into the fish and save the rest for serving.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Serve separately or add to taste.

ingredients.name: Fresh rice vermicelli
ingredients.notes: Serve on the side; briefly blanch if needed.

preparation_steps: Blanch the pork bones for 3 minutes, discard the water and rinse the bones. Put them in a pot with the daikon, shallots and fresh water; keep chilled if not simmering immediately.

Keep the fish paste cold. Mix it with some fish sauce, pepper and scallions; knead in one direction for 5–7 minutes until sticky and elastic. Shape into bite-size balls and chill while the broth simmers.
Halve the bitter melon, remove the pith and slice. Clean the mushrooms and prepare the vermicelli and hotpot greens away from the raw fish-preparation area.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones and daikon over low heat for 40–45 minutes, skimming regularly to keep the broth clear. Remove the larger bones if desired, then season with salt and the remaining fish sauce.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil and add the fish balls. Cook for 5–7 minutes until they float and are cooked through; add the mushrooms and cook for 3 more minutes.
Move the pot to the table burner. Add bitter melon in batches and cook until just tender but still green. Finish with scallions and serve with rice vermicelli and fish sauce with chili.

banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.name: Hà Giang hunchback bánh chưng
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.serving_basis: Four small hunchback-shaped cakes, one per person or halved for a festive meal.
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.description: Bánh chưng gù is a small hand-wrapped sticky-rice cake associated with the Tày people of Hà Giang. Bếp Việt adapts the Ngọc Đường style using rice naturally tinted green with leaf ginger, mung beans and pork belly wrapped in dong leaves and simmered until the rice is tender. It requires advance preparation and long cooking.
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.finished_dish: Small hand-wrapped cakes have a softly curved hunchback shape and deep-green dong leaves; the cut face shows naturally green sticky rice around a savory mung-bean and pork-belly filling.
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.serving: Let the cakes drain and cool slightly before cutting into halves or thick slices. Serve warm with pickled onions or pickled vegetables, or as a filling breakfast during Tết.
tips: Soak the rice and mung beans separately; drain them well before wrapping so the cakes cook evenly without becoming wet.
Wrap each cake tightly by hand into a small curved shape, but do not compress the rice so firmly that it cannot expand; tie the leaves securely.
Keep the cakes submerged in water for 8–10 hours and top up with boiling water as needed; never let the pot run dry or expose the cakes.
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.image_alt: Small Hà Giang bánh chưng gù wrapped in dong leaves, one cut to show naturally green leaf-ginger rice with mung-bean and pork filling; Bếp Việt image on a transparent background.
banh-chung-gu-ha-giang.time_note: About 16 hours in total, including 6 hours of soaking and 9 hours of boiling; soak the rice and beans ahead.

ingredients.name: Upland glutinous rice
ingredients.notes: Rinse gently, soak for 6 hours and drain; choose fresh sticky rice.

ingredients.name: Split mung beans
ingredients.notes: Soak separately for 2 hours and drain; steam briefly for a fluffy filling if desired.

ingredients.name: Pork belly
ingredients.notes: Cut into four long strips for the filling.

ingredients.name: Dong leaves
ingredients.notes: Choose flexible leaves, wash and dry; use scraps as extra lining if needed.

ingredients.name: Leaf ginger
ingredients.notes: Blend with about 100 ml water and strain to obtain green coloring liquid.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For blending the leaf ginger; prepare additional hot water separately for boiling.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Season the pork; choose a moderately salty sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Divide between the rice, beans and boiling water to taste.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Freshly grind and season the pork.

ingredients.name: Bamboo ties
ingredients.notes: Soak until pliable if dry; use to secure the cakes.

preparation_steps: Rinse the sticky rice gently, soak for 6 hours and drain. Soak the mung beans separately for 2 hours. Blend and strain the leaf ginger, mix the green liquid with the rice and some salt, then let the color absorb for about 20 minutes.
Season the pork belly with fish sauce, pepper and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes. For a fluffy filling, steam the mung beans until just tender and let them cool.

Wipe the dong leaves dry and overlap two leaves in opposite directions. Spread a layer of green rice, add the mung beans and a pork strip in the center, cover with rice, then fold by hand into a small curved cake and tie it securely.
cooking_steps: Line the bottom of a pot with spare dong leaves, arrange the cakes snugly and pour in boiling water to cover. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat to a steady simmer.
Boil continuously for about 8–10 hours depending on cake size. Add boiling water as the level drops and keep the cakes fully submerged; reposition them if the pot heats unevenly.
Lift out the cakes, briefly rinse the leaf surface with warm clean water and drain. Press under a moderate weight for 20–30 minutes to firm the surface, then cool slightly before cutting.
